anomalies.observed: On the right-hand side of the sheet, D2 (PMEG3030EP, '3A 360mV') is drawn vertically with its cathode bar on the top terminal, which is tied to the +5V global net, and its anode on the bottom terminal, which feeds the servo power rail (the node that runs to J3 pin 2, J8 pin 2 and the C1-C4 bank). This orients the Schottky so that it blocks current from +5V into the servo rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification states D2 is the 'Diode from +5V into the servo power rail (feeding J3/J8 pin 2 and the C1-C4 bank)', i.e. anode on the +5V side and cathode on the servo-rail side so that +5V forward-biases the diode and powers the servos.

evidence.quote: D2 PMEG3030EP 3A 360mV - cathode (bar) at the +5V arrow, anode at the servo-rail node feeding J3 pin2/J8 pin2 and C1-C4 (sheet m5-pantilt, right column)
D2 | PMEG3030EP Schottky ... Diode from `+5V` into the servo power rail (feeding J3/J8 pin 2 and the C1-C4 bank)

anomalies.impact: With the Schottky reversed, the +5V rail cannot forward-bias D2, so the dedicated servo power rail (J3/J8 pin 2 and C1-C4) is never energised from +5V. The pan/tilt servos would receive no supply in either PWM or Serial mode, and the bulk-capacitor inrush buffering described in the spec would be defeated.
